intent: Lay out two or more panels side by side or stacked, with draggable handles between them that let the user resize the panels.
typical_uses: A split view whose panes the user sizes directly, such as a list beside a detail view
A multi-pane workspace with both horizontal and vertical splits

dont_use_when.situation: A layout with fixed proportions that the user never resizes

instead.target: a plain flex or grid container styled by the application
instead.note: The group only adds value through its handles; without them it is a flex container with the library's layout bookkeeping on top.

dont_use_when.situation: A side navigation that opens and closes from a toggle rather than being dragged to a size

invariants.text: Panels and handles must be direct DOM children of the group's element, as the wrapped library requires; a wrapper element between the group and a panel or handle breaks that requirement.

The group renders a div whose inline `display: flex`, `flex-direction` (row for `orientation="horizontal"`, the default, column for `vertical`) and `flex-wrap: nowrap` are set from `orientation` after `style` is applied, so neither `style` nor `className` can change them. Its inline width and height default to 100% of the parent and its overflow to hidden; `style` may override those three.

There is no controlled layout prop: `defaultLayout` seeds the panel sizes, keyed by each panel's `id`; later changes are reported through `onLayoutChange` while they happen and `onLayoutChanged` once they settle, and are set from outside only through the imperative handle on `groupRef`.
The group, every panel and every handle write their resolved `id` into `data-testid` after the consumer's attributes, so a consumer `data-testid` is overwritten.

anti_patterns.dont: Pass `data-testid` to the group or its parts to find them in a test
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `id` and query by it, or query a handle by its separator role

children.states: children are the group's panels and the handles between them
children.because: `ReactNode` covers elements, strings, arrays and more, and the compiler emits one JSON type per property; which components belong here is stated by `accepts`.

defaultLayout.states: defaultLayout is an object mapping each panel's `id` to its starting size
defaultLayout.because: The library's `Layout` is `{ [id: string]: number }`, a map keyed by panel ids the caller chooses; the compiler leaves the named type to tsc.

elementRef.states: elementRef is a ref to the group's div element
elementRef.because: `Ref<HTMLDivElement | null>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

groupRef.states: groupRef receives the group's imperative handle, with getLayout and setLayout
groupRef.because: `Ref<GroupImperativeHandle | null>` is a ref object or a callback holding an object of functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

onLayoutChange.states: onLayoutChange is a callback called with the layout on every change while the user drags or presses a resize key, not a value
onLayoutChange.because: `(layout: Layout) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

onLayoutChanged.states: onLayoutChanged is a callback called with the layout and a meta object once a change settles, not a value
onLayoutChanged.because: `(layout: Layout, meta: LayoutChangedMeta) => void`, where `meta.isUserInteraction` tells a pointer or keyboard resize from any other cause - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

resizeTargetMinimumSize.states: resizeTargetMinimumSize is an object with a `coarse` and a `fine` number, the minimum hit-target size for touch and for mouse input
resizeTargetMinimumSize.because: `{ coarse: number; fine: number }` is an inline object type, which the compiler leaves to tsc.

style.states: style is a plain style object applied inline to the group's div
style.because: `CSSProperties` is React's style object type, which the compiler leaves to tsc. The group sets `display`, `flex-direction` and `flex-wrap` after it, so those three cannot be overridden; the kit's own styling goes through resizable.module.css.

good.title: A two-panel horizontal split with a visible grip
A vertical split nested inside one panel of a horizontal split

bad.title: The orientation prop name of an older library version
bad.why: The group takes `orientation`, not `direction`; an unknown `direction` lands on the div as an attribute and the panels stay side by side.

bad.title: A panel wrapped in an extra element
bad.why: Panels and handles must be direct children of the group's element.
